devices.notes: Numbers from arXiv v1 (2609.24611v1, 10 pages, 21 Sep 2026); Supplementary Sections I-IX are not in the cached source. Phase-shifting mechanism is carrier accumulation and depletion (plasma dispersion, band filling, Franz-Keldysh) in n-InGaAsP, not Pockels; eo_material=other. VpiL 0.13 V*cm measured on 500 and 1000 um phase shifters (Fig. 2(d)); Vpi 2.2 V is quoted for 600 um without stating how it was obtained (not described as a measurement); consistent with 0.13 V*cm / 0.6 mm = 2.17 V. p.5 also gives 2.3 V as approximately Vpi for 600 um. Wavelength 1550 nm. Fig. 2(e) MZI with 1.1 mm phase shifter shows more than 2 pi tuning (gate -1 to 5 V). Dynamic: 10-90% rise 555 ps and fall 417 ps, 9.375 MHz square wave, 2.0 Vpp on 3.0 V bias (Fig. 2(f)), device length not stated; RC-limited; no S21 bandwidth reported. Static power 28.9 fW/pi (13.3 fA leakage, 600 um); circuit median 21.8 fW; switching energy 15.3 pJ/pi (C = 6.48 pF); not mapped to energy_per_bit_fj (per pi, not per bit). Carrier-induced excess loss 0.20 dB/pi; taper loss 0.18 dB each; il_onchip_db is the section total at pi, loss reference and normalization defined in Supplementary Sections IV-V (not read). Circuit: 4x4 Clements mesh, channel crosstalk below -12 dB, 50 random unitaries R2 0.93, negligible thermal crosstalk. MZI internal and external phase-shifter pairs operated push-pull in the circuit. Phase-shifter drive mode, ER and rib width not reported.

devices.notes: Modulator #1 (narrow gap). EO 3 dB bandwidth 84 GHz is measured (3.6 dB roll-off at 100 GHz; VNA to 67 GHz plus OSA 60-100 GHz); the roll-off reference is 'low frequencies' (Fig. 5), no frequency stated. Data demonstrations (Fig. 8) are specified for modulator #1 (Sec. 3.4, Fig. 8(a)) although the abstract says 'these modulators'. 100 Gbaud OOK BER 8.5e-6; PAM-4 106.25 Gb/s BER below 1e-6, 200 Gb/s BER 5.5e-3; PAM-8 240 Gb/s BER 1.1e-2 (below the 2e-2 SD-FEC limit). Energy: Vrms 656 mV gives 81 fJ/bit (PAM-4 106.25 Gb/s), Vrms 1.23 V gives 124 fJ/bit (PAM-8 240 Gb/s), authors' estimates without stated driver impedance. D = 0.6 um, Wg = 40 um, Tc = 0.8 um, Tb = 0.2 um. Line parameters (Fig. 4) are reported only for modulator #2. Fig. 5(a): trace scatters about -3 dB from about 75 to 100 GHz; deepest about -3.5 dB near 97 GHz (approx. reading).

Mechanism: ITO carrier accumulation/depletion in a MOS capacitor with plasmonic enhancement from the Au top plate (not Pockels); drive +/-3.5 V (7 V swing), carrier density 1.6e20 to 2.5e20 cm-3 in 10 nm ITO. devices.notes: Single device characterized (124 um modulation region per arm, Fig. 3a). All values from the arXiv v1 preprint, not the Science Advances VoR; Supplement not cached. Not reported in the preprint: Vpi, Vpi*L, measured modulation efficiency (so vpi_convention empty), drive amplitude, bias voltage, optical input power, Z0 value, n_RF, RF loss, energy per bit, capacitance, temperature; no per-length propagation loss entered. Design-stage values not entered as device metrics (simulated, Sec. 2 and Fig. 2): efficiency factor 0.013 pi/V at the design point (voltage not stated), optical bandwidth about 140 GHz, electrical bandwidth about 200 GHz at 4 V, Q_propagating about 5000; Fig. 2(g) shows simulated electrode loss for 124 um. Bandwidth: 110 GHz is the crossing of the authors' fit to the S21 curve (Fig. 4c; basis derived, not a direct trace crossing); measured trace spans 0 to 110 GHz and reaches about -3 to -4 dB at the end, so the crossing sits at the instrument limit (bw_measured_to_ghz = 110). Curve starts at 0 dB at low frequency, hence reference dc (derived); it shows about +1.5 dB peaking near 20 GHz (read from figure). Authors say the result is slightly degraded by RF probe loss; de-embedding, bias, operating wavelength and the dB convention of S21 (electrical or optical) are not stated. Wavelength 1550 nm is nominal: the mid-gap passband is about 8 nm wide around 1550 nm (design 11 nm), data wavelengths span 1548-1556 nm (Fig. 4f-g); wavelength of the S21 measurement not stated. ER is the dynamic ER at 112 Gb/s (2.15 dB); 3.15 dB at 100 Gb/s (Fig. 4d caption); ER, OMA and SNR vary by less than 0.5 dB across the passband (Fig. 4f). Data rate: OOK so baud equals bit rate (derived); text says BER is below HD-FEC (3.8e-3) up to 98 Gb/s and below SD-FEC (2e-3) up to 112 Gb/s, but in Fig. 4h the 20 percent FEC line reads about 1.5e-2 and the best 112 Gb/s point about 1.7e-2 (figure reading), so the SD-FEC claim is not confirmed from the figure; max_line_rate_gbps 112 is the demonstrated line rate (eyes and BER measured), not an FEC-compliant rate (BER is below the 7 percent HD-FEC line only up to 98 Gb/s), and no net rate is entered. Insertion loss: 6.8 dB on-chip with 5.4 dB from the phase shifter (Methods p.15); wording of the excluded coupling loss is ambiguous.

Operating point: 3 dB IL at -1.5 V, bias -1.9 V, swing -1.5 to -2.3 V (0.8 Vpp). Static ER 6 dB is read on the transmission-vs-gate-voltage curve within that swing, not from eye diagrams. Tuning efficiency 117 pm/V applies in accumulation mode (beyond -1.5 V); 87 pm/V in depletion mode (0 to -1.5 V). Vpi*L 0.12 V cm is a resonance-shift figure (formula not given; FSR not stated, so not re-derived). 3 dB bandwidth 11 GHz includes optical peaking, referenced to 500 MHz, RC-limited by 500 fF total capacitance; the text states the photon-lifetime limit as 50 GHz (Q 4600). Capacitance 333 fF is the authors' total (500 fF) minus the slab contribution; leakage 495 pA at -1.9 V (SI). Energy 53 fJ/bit is the authors' C*V^2/4 with 333 fF and 0.8 Vpp (checks to 53.3). 25 Gb/s open eye at 0.8 Vpp without pre-emphasis; 35 Gb/s open eyes need 1.75 Vpp and AWG pre-emphasis from the S21 data. Passive ring Q about 20000 near critical coupling (design target in text). Simulated values (Q 5000, 125 pm/V, 7.6 dB ER) are not entered. Not reported: FSR, coupling gap, BOX thickness, on-chip optical power, temperature, fiber coupling loss, Vpi in volts, dynamic ER.

devices.notes: Version: all values from arXiv 2111.05331v1 (15 pp, preprint titled 'Beyond 300Gbps Silicon Microring Modulator with AI Acceleration'), not the Communications Engineering version of record (title differs; Crossref title used). Two rows by operating point (convention d): -a data run at -0.9 V / 1312 nm, -b the optical-peaking bandwidth point. Fig. 5(b) is the system frequency response of the whole optical link (AWG, amplifier, probe, device, photodetector) at -0.9 V, labelled -3 dB EO bandwidth 42.5 GHz (text: approximately), normalized at the 1 GHz plot start; peaking at 30 GHz. Vpi*L 0.8 V cm is stated in the design paragraph as 'remains as high as' with characterization deferred to ref. [34]; bias and definition not given; the value is not tied to the -0.9 V / 1312 nm operating point, basis author_estimate, qualifier approx because 'as high as' gives no clear bound direction. drive_vpp_v 0.6: Vpp is fixed at 600 mV in the Fig. 5(c),(d) data-rate scans, which peak near 302 Gb/s at 1312.0 nm and -0.9 V (p.8); the Fig. 7 / Methods run states no Vpp. 302 Gb/s is the back-to-back BPL-DMT rate at 60 GBaud (256 subcarriers, 8 zero-padded removed, SE about 5.20 bit/s/Hz), received power 7 dBm, BER under the 20 percent SD-FEC threshold 2e-2 with the Bi-GRU equalizer; 300 Gb/s over 1 km SSMF (SE about 5.16). No net rate entered (FEC overhead not netted by the authors). Fiber grating-coupler efficiency about 40 percent (Methods). Inconsistency: the Methods parameter-extraction simulation uses ring radius 10 um while the device is 8 um; text says 'etching a 220-nm width Si waveguide' (read as the 220 nm SOI thickness, consistent with 150 nm etch + 70 nm slab in Fig. 1(b)). Not reported: junction length, doping beyond 3e18 cm^-3, Q, tuning efficiency, extinction ratio, insertion loss, energy per bit, on-chip optical power, foundry.

devices.notes: Version: all values from arXiv 2509.01555v1 (55 pp incl. Supplementary Information), not the Laser & Photonics Reviews version of record. One physical device (8 um radius ring, 40 um doped region); two rows split by operating point (0 V self-biasing here, -3 V depletion in hu2026-b). Static spectral values (Q, FSR, ER, IL, tuning, Vpi*L) sit on this row only. Fig. 3(d) EO S21 curves are normalized; reference frequency of the 3 dB drop not stated. 3 dB BW at 0 V is operating-point dependent (83, 97, more than 110 GHz at 6, 5, 4 dB IL, optical peaking); wafer map (9 dies, 6 dB point, Fig. 3(e)) reads 81.8 to 93.6 GHz at 0 V (text says above 82 GHz; centre die 83.6). Vpi*L is a resonance-shift-derived figure (0 to -4 V average), not a phase-shifter Vpi. Junction Rs about 31 ohm at 0 V (simulated, p.39). Heater 81.2 pm/mW. Temperature: normalized OMA of a 64 GBd NRZ eye over a 1.5 K range (p.45, Fig. S6). Optical power at the 32 Gb/s demo: Rop 3 dBm for BER below 1e-12 (p.15); PCIe 5.0 eye width meets 9.375 ps. Not reported: Vpi at a single bias, RF Vpi, doping levels, BOX thickness, cladding, fabricator name (12-inch CMOS foundry), on-chip optical power for data runs, temperature class, BER values for the PAM4 and 180 GBd eyes. drive_vpp_v is the authors' estimated swing at the DUT (cable attenuation factor, Fig. S10), not an on-chip measurement.

Co-packaged transmitter: 150 um Si photonic-crystal-waveguide MZM (design same as the authors' earlier Optica 2024 paper) plus the driver. Row -a is the nominal ng = 35 +/- 5 spectral point near 1537 nm; wavelength is the reference wavelength stated for the ng spread, the laser wavelength of the data runs is not stated. 3 dB bandwidth 50 GHz is the tunable-peaking-ON label for ng = 35 in Fig. 4(c) (peaking OFF: 42 GHz); the EO sweep covered 1 to 40 GHz at PDC 260 mW with the whole transmitter (driver, bond wires), and the labelled crossing sits on the co-simulated curve beyond the measured range, so bw_measured_to is 40 and the basis is simulated (a crossing read on the co-simulation curve beyond the measured range). The 50 GHz bandwidth is at PDC = 260 mW with peaking ON for the whole transmitter; it is not the bandwidth of the 50 mW / 0.78 pJ/bit operating point, whose bandwidth is not reported (ER 1.4 dB and energy are at 50 mW). Row mixes these two operating points; no separate row is split out. Energy 0.78 pJ/bit = 50 mW / 64 Gb/s with a 5-tap receiver FFE (SD-FEC compatible); DSP-free best 1.0 pJ/bit (50 Gb/s, 50 mW); with laser (80 mW at assumed 20% WPE) and bias control (3.3 mW) the total rises to 133 mW and 2.1 pJ/bit. Extinction ratio 1.4 dB is that of the unprocessed 64 Gb/s eye at 50 mW (4.0 dB at 260 mW). Active footprint 0.66 mm^2 (modulator 0.3 mm^2); on-chip insertion loss about 11 dB including about 8 dB from the PN-doped PCW phase shifter; PCW 3 dB operating bandwidth 5.9 nm; 2.6 nm spectral shift from 0 to 300 mW (25 to 84 C simulated); quadrature bias heater at most 3.3 mW. Z0 about 50 ohm is the simulated electrode impedance (LH raises it from 30 ohm). Laser 13 dBm is the tunable-laser output (coupling loss not stated); the source amplitude to the driver was 0.4 Vpp (not the modulator swing). Not reported: Vpi, modulator-level drive swing, electrode dimensions, doping, junction capacitance, temperature class. bw3db_reference 1ghz is derived: Fig. 4(c) is normalized and the sweep starts at 1 GHz, but the normalization frequency is not stated.

devices.notes: Version: arXiv 2506.04820v1. Same transmitter as kawahara2025-a at a different spectral (wavelength) point: ng = 30 with tunable driver peaking ON gives the widest bandwidth, 55 GHz (Table 1 'This Work' 55 GHz; text 'recorded'). Label read on Fig. 4(c) at PDC = 260 mW; EO sweep covered 1 to 40 GHz with the labelled crossing on the co-simulated curve beyond it (basis simulated) (peaking OFF 46 GHz; ng = 40: 38 GHz OFF, 45 GHz ON, text and figure). Wavelength of the ng = 30 point is not stated. The text infers potential for operation beyond 100 Gbaud; no data above 64 Gb/s was taken.

devices.notes: Headline device (abstract: RF Vpi 1.3 V at 1 GHz, 1.8 dB roll-off at 50 GHz). Vpi at 50 GHz 1.6 V is stated by the authors (1.3 V plus 1.8 dB) and not entered. The 1.35 V is called DC in the text and the Fig. 3 caption but labelled 1 MHz in the plot. ER is explicitly for the 20 mm device (Fig. 3(a)); on-chip and total insertion loss are not attributed to a device in the text and are entered here as the headline device. No 3 dB bandwidth stated: the Fig. 3(b) trace touches the -3 dB line near 46 GHz (noise) while the authors give 1.8 dB at 50 GHz, so no bound is entered. Authors extrapolate a conductor-loss-limited 3 dB bandwidth of about 180 GHz for 20 mm (Fig. 4a, p.5; prediction, not a column). Sub-volt >100 GHz is a design projection, not a device. Numbers from arXiv v1.

devices.modulation_format: 4-QAM (2 bits/symbol) from two binary-driven cavities, 2^7-1 PRBS, 20 MHz to 1 GHz modulation frequency, EVM below 0.27 (average over symbols) up to near the 3 dB cutoff
devices.notes: One physical device. No Vpi (resonant device, tuning efficiency instead). Per-cavity fit (Table I p.4, fitted to Fig. 3b,c and 4b): Q 6.6e4 / 7.4e4, total linewidth 2.9 / 2.6 GHz (cavity 1 / 2), kappa_c/kappa_i 0.46 / 1.42, tuning 1.15 / 1.09 GHz/V; first-order perturbation theory gives 1.0 GHz/V (p.3, Supp VI). Row tuning 0.0092 nm/V is the cavity-1 slope read from Fig. 3b (cavity 2: 8.7 pm/V, Fig. 3c); q_loaded 70000 is the paper approximate value (text p.2). 3 dB cutoff around 1.5 GHz for each cavity (Fig. 4a, small-signal, plotted 0 to 5 GHz, matches the fitted linewidths); reference entered as dc (curve normalised at 0 GHz, not stated by the authors). ER: more than 30 dB at the two destructive-interference minima of |t_IQ|^2 (Fig. 4b inset, p.3), static. 4-QAM drive: +-1 V on each cavity (2 V peak to peak, p.2; p.3); no baud rate stated (the modulation frequency 1 GHz is not identified as a symbol rate), so max_baud and line rate left empty. Energy 25.8 fJ/bit = 51.5 fJ/symbol / 2 bits from a COMSOL Maxwell capacitance matrix (C11 10.6, C12 9.4, C22 22.2 fF) and a 0D circuit simulation with 0-2 V swing (Supp VI p.19), an author estimate. Geometry: 600 nm film, 400 nm etch (slab 200 nm derived), 35 deg outer sidewall and about 17 deg inner sidewall in the Bragg gaps (p.6), waveguide 800 nm tapering to 900 nm in the PhC, Bragg period 426 nm, 660 nm directional-coupler gap, 12:88 measured splitting ratio at 1548.65 nm (Supp Fig. 3, p.14). Electrode gap not stated in text. Facet insertion loss 8.2 dB (15 percent transmission, faulty facet etch; about 3 dB in other runs) in Supp IX p.26 is not entered because the paper does not define it as on-chip or fiber-to-fiber loss. Fabrication yield 64 percent: 18 of 28 resonant two-sided cavities (of 51 measured) with Q above 2e4 (Supp Fig. 11, p.18). Coherent receiver (AIM Photonics silicon PIC) limited detection to 2 GHz. Sidewall angle 35 deg is measured from the chip normal as stated on p.6 (55 deg from the film plane); other rows in the atlas may use the film plane. Fig. 4a draws both -3 dB and -6 dB reference lines and the paper does not state whether dB is optical or electrical power; the 1.5 GHz matches the -3 dB line and the fitted linewidths.

devices.notes: Vpi 4.2 V measured with a 400 kHz triangular drive (quasi-DC, avoids drift) as the voltage swing between minimum and maximum transmission; push-pull GSG convention stated on p.4 and in the Fig. 4 caption. VpiL 85 +- 2 mV cm uses the 200 um electrode length (six devices, sd 2 mV cm); simulated VpiL 96 +- 2 mV cm with r33 35 pm/V. 3 dB bandwidth 922 MHz is the electrical-optical-electrical link response including a 900 MHz APD (detector-limited, not subtracted), so it is entered as a lower bound (bw3db_ghz:gt) for the modulator and the 3 dB reference level is not stated. EO roll-off 1 dB at 67 GHz is the authors estimate from the electrical S21 (2 dB attenuation at 67 GHz), RF loss and velocity mismatch with a 23 ohm termination, not a measured EO response; reference level not stated. Z0 23 ohm and n_rf 2.3 (single value in the text, no frequency given; the Fig. 5(e) curve falls from about 5 at low frequency to a plateau of about 2.5, visual reading +-0.1, from about 20 to 67 GHz, so it is strongly frequency dependent below about 15 GHz) are extracted from measured S-parameters of the lumped electrodes; ng 2.8 is the calculated optical group index. IL 1.3 dB is the authors combination of measured MMI loss (3.25 dB each, includes the 3 dB split, simulated 3.11 dB) and propagation loss (formula not given; batch check 2 x 0.25 + 7.2 dB/cm x 0.116 cm = 1.34 dB if the split is excluded); the 200 um phase shifter alone contributes 0.14 dB. Propagation loss 7.2 dB/cm at 375 nm (spirals; 2 dB/cm at 780 nm); film absorption 1.32 dB/cm at 443 nm on 600 nm film. No photodarkening at 5 kW/mm2 calculated from 700 uW guided power (p.13): entered as optical_power_handling_dbm lower bound (10 log10 0.7 mW = -1.55 dBm). p.12 also reports record-low VpiL 0.085 V cm at 375 nm and 0.12 V cm at 448 nm (Fig. 6a); the 448 nm point has no stated device, Vpi or length (the second this-work marker in Fig. 6a is plotted near 485 nm), so it is not a row. Fig. 4(e) image (caption (d)) also shows measured VpiL about 0.12 V cm at 2.0 um and 0.16 V cm at 2.5 um gap (visual; no Vpi or length). Not reported: BOX thickness, substrate, electrode widths, cladding, capacitance, RF drive for data, optical input power at chip.

devices.notes: VERSION arXiv v1. Folded layout with waveguide crossing: two 5.5 mm interaction sections (11 mm total), physical length 7.8 mm; output 2x2 MMI gives two complementary outputs. Vpi 2.98 V from a 150 kHz triangular sweep (Fig. 7(f)); abstract says less than 3.0 V; Vpi*L 3.3 V cm is the abstract value (2.98 V x 11 mm = 3.28). EO response measured as optical sidebands 3-40 GHz at 1550 nm with UV15 present (Fig. 11); text: roll-off about 0.1 dB/GHz, 3 dB bandwidth roughly 30 GHz (3 dB divided by the rounded 0.1 dB/GHz slope, entered as derived); low frequencies omitted because of unlevel RF source, so the reference frequency is not defined. Fig. 11 fitted slopes 0.108-0.137 dB/GHz. RF index: UV15-clad about 2.10, air-clad about 1.85 (p.5, Fig. 5(c); these are the values near 40 GHz, UV15 falls from about 2.4 at 1 GHz to about 2.13 at 20 GHz, air-clad from about 2.1 to 1.89 at 10 GHz); optical group index about 2.14 (simulated); electrode impedance 43-53 ohm over 5-40 GHz in Fig. 5(d), not entered (one-line curve). Text says electrode S21 at 40 GHz is roughly -3 dB (air) and -4 dB (UV15), but Fig. 5(a),(b) show S(1,2) about -5.8 dB (air) and -7.2 dB (UV15) at 40 GHz (text and figure disagree); electrode length not stated. ER 45 dB: OSA peak-to-null in Fig. 8 gives 45.5 dB (port 1) and 45.4 dB (port 2); power meter reads higher, the lower OSA value used; reverse operation about 33 dB. Fiber-to-fiber loss 12.0 dB = 2 x 4.44 dB coupling + 1.1 dB path + 2.02 dB alignment (author accounting). Ground width 75 um. Thermo-optic bias P_pi 92 mW. Fabricator not named.

devices.notes: Four-channel DR4 chip, 5.1 x 3.5 mm2 die, 1.75 mm phase shifters, 50 ohm differential on-chip terminations, thermal phase shifters (P_pi 13 mW), Ge monitor photodiodes. Row values are for the bare BTO die (Vpi, EO S21, DC ER) or system level (all four channels reach 225 GBd PAM4). Vpi 6 V is called 'differential Vpi of the bare die'; whether it is a DC or a low-frequency value is not stated, so it is entered in vpi_dc_v with that caveat. EO S21 normalised to 1 GHz (Fig. 1b caption): 3 dB 55 GHz, 6 dB 105 GHz; the figure itself was not available. Loss: connectorised fiber-to-fiber 12.5-14 dB across channels (includes 1-2.5 dB splice loss), of which the PIC contributes 11.5 dB (6 dB 1x4 laser power splitter, 1.25 dB per fiber edge coupler, 3 dB on-chip IL); no single fiber-to-fiber value is entered because it is a per-channel range; only the 3 dB on-chip figure is entered, excluding the splitter and couplers. A stated 448 Gbps PAM4 line-rate figure (title, Sec. 1, Sec. 5) is deliberately not entered in max_line_rate_gbps (the results give net rates). Wavelength not stated beyond O-band. System: all four channels 225 GBd PAM4 under HD-FEC over 2 km SSMF with Tx pre-emphasis, Rx DFE and 1-tap MLSE (net 422 Gb/s per lane); PAM6 net 506 and PAM8 net 540 Gb/s at 225 GBd; 112 GBd PAM4 BER below 1e-6 (DFE only); stable to 85 degC (TEC limit), slight degradation above 50 degC attributed to driver gain; one channel driven at a time, crosstalk negligible; drivers roll off 15 dB beyond 105 GHz (Fig. 2b); 2 dBm Tx average power; 20 dBm QD DFB laser split on chip. BTO is grown by MBE on silicon and transferred onto processed SiPh wafers; the text also calls the integration monolithic, so integration is entered as other. Not reported: wavelength, Vpi frequency or bias, electrode type/geometry, propagation or RF loss, Z0, n_rf, ng, film thickness, energy per bit.

devices.notes: Single device. All numbers from the publisher-formatted KIT repository copy of the JLT article (17 PDF pages, 2026 IEEE notice; license not verifiable from the copy or from Crossref, so redistribution stays restricted_local_only). Vpi 2.4 V measured, 0.67 V mm reported (stored as 0.067 V cm); measurement frequency and wavelength of the Vpi value not stated; MZM in push-pull (Appendix, p.15). Bandwidth: 3 dB 74 GHz and 6 dB beyond 110 GHz from the EO transfer function normalized to 70 kHz, smoothed with a 10 GHz moving average, calibrated 110 GHz photodiode, probe and cables removed, 50 ohm termination, measured to 110 GHz (Fig. 3c); no gate voltage is mentioned. The simulated response (Fig. 3c) is not entered. On-chip IL 2.7 dB at 1550 nm from fringe fits of a 40 um imbalanced MZM, grating coupler removed; phase-shifter loss 0.9 dB (author deduction by subtraction, Table I) equals 3.2 dB/mm over 0.28 mm, stored as 32 dB/cm with derived basis. ER 38 dB from the same spectrum (static). Z0 about 49.2 ohm is the real part of the simulated line impedance (frequency not stated); RF line S21 -5.5 dB at 110 GHz over the 320 um line, S11 below -15 dB to 110 GHz (measured, not converted to dB/cm). Author-derived: field-interaction factor 0.185 (simulated, TEM geometry), in-device r33 158 pm/V; nOEO 1.8. Geometry cells: rib width 240 nm is the design value (TEM 250 nm at base or about 230 nm per caption), slab 75 nm and sidewall angle about 10 deg are TEM values of a raw device; the 3 um BOX appears only in the generic platform schematic Fig. 1c and is not entered. Data experiment at 1556 nm, 13 dBm laser (not on-chip power), 1.7 dBm fiber output power, drive voltage not stated; BER examples: PAM4 192 GBd 4.8e-3, PAM6 176 GBd 1.9e-2, PAM8 176 GBd 3.4e-2 (electrical back-to-back 2.2e-2). Net data rates by authors from FEC implementations of ref. [59]: 412.5 Gbit/s at 160 GBd PAM8 (line rate 480 Gbit/s), 410 Gbit/s at 176 GBd PAM8, 375.9 Gbit/s PAM6 176 GBd, 356.5 Gbit/s PAM4 192 GBd. PAM6 maximum symbol rate is stated as 180 GBd (abstract, summary, 465 Gbit/s) and as 184 GBd (Sec. IV, 476 Gbit/s); max_baud uses the PAM4 value 204 GBd. Foundry not named, so foundry_or_fab is empty. Not reported: RF Vpi, n_RF, optical group index, energy per bit, drive amplitude, on-chip optical input power, signal-electrode width and thickness, doping levels.

The 18 GHz, 50 Gbps and 0.85 V cm quoted in the batch hint are not in the cached text and are not used. 3 dB bandwidth: Fig. 4(a) -2 V trace crosses -3 dB near 15 to 16 GHz (-1 V trace near 13.5 GHz); the text says 'beyond 15 GHz', so 15 with qualifier gt; response normalized at the 0 GHz plot start (reference dc, derived). devices.notes: Version: arXiv 2210.06994v1 (9 pp, IEEE template placeholder header), no journal DOI located. Ring-assisted MZM (racetrack phase shifter on one arm of a symmetric MZI), measured at Vbias = 1 V reverse (paper quotes the magnitude; negative sign here follows the repo reverse-bias convention). SFDR 75 dB Hz^(2/3) (Fig. 9(a), carrier-injection-like nonlinearity). Vpi*L 0.70 V cm is the low end of the stated range. Bandwidth is measured with a 17.5 GHz photodetector; the response shows optical peaking and is normalized at the lowest frequency (about 1 GHz), reference unspecified. Static ER 21.5 dB and FSR 7.7 nm are measured at Vbias = 0 V (Fig. 4(a)) and are carried on the 1 V row only. Racetrack straight 2.25 um, gap 0.2 um, power coupling 0.77 (simulated, overcoupled by design); MZI arm 375 um (not the phase-shifter length); PN junction covers 44 percent of the 180-degree bends; 99 percent of the mode lies in the P/N regions (overlap analysis). Vpi*L definition and active length are not stated, so no length or Vpi is entered. Fabricator not named (platform said to be commercially available; one author is at CompoundTek). Not reported: insertion loss, Vpi in volts, active length, energy, optical power, wavelength tolerance. No 0 V row exists: the static ER 21.5 dB and FSR 7.7 nm are Vbias = 0 V values although bias_for_vpi_v here is -1 V.

Transduction (not columns): microwave resonance 6.672 GHz (lambda/4 CPW, about 100 ohm, 5200 um), conversion efficiency 2.2e-9 at -26 dBm pump and -31 dBm RF, conversion bandwidth 20.3 MHz, sideband contrast 9.5 dB, g0/2pi 330 +/- 60 Hz inferred and 400 Hz predicted (Table 1, p.19). devices.notes: Version: all values from arXiv 2312.14537v1 (19 pp), no journal DOI; no Crossref record. Dual-drive MZM whose two carrier-depletion phase shifters are set to different bandwidths by bias; the equalization factor EF is the low-speed to high-speed drive amplitude ratio. Open-eye OOK baud rate without DSP rises with EF: 30 GBd at EF 0 (ER 3.59 dB), 60 at 0.36, 80 at 0.61, 90 at 0.75 (Fig. 6; ER 2.29 dB at 90 GBd for EF 0.75). Drive: 3.6 Vpp on the high-speed shifter at 6 V bias; low-speed shifter 1.3, 2.2, 2.7 Vpp at EF 0.36, 0.61, 0.75, bias kept below 4 V. 50 um arm path-length difference lets the carrier wavelength set the operating point. Relation to yue2025 (2410.09816, tunable time-frequency equalization, over 110 GHz, 140 GBd): related technique from the same group but a different, later paper with different devices and numbers; yue2023 is not cited in the cached yue2025 PDF. Numbers are kept separate. Step-response simulations (Figs. 2-3, assumed 60/20 GHz phase-shifter bandwidths) are illustrative and not entered. Not reported: Vpi, EO S21, wavelength, doping levels, optical power.

papers.label: Anderson et al. 2025
papers.notes: VERSION: all numbers come from the cached arXiv v1 (2502.15164v1, 24 pp including Supplementary Information, page-1 stamp 2025-02-21). The Science version of record (390(6771) 394-399, issued 2025-10-23 per Crossref) was not read and may differ. License of the preprint unverified (Crossref record carries no license), so license and published_on are empty; batch-hint CC-BY-4.0 not verifiable. MATERIAL-ONLY, no device rows: bulk SrTiO3 (STO) crystals (5x5 mm chips, 0.5 or 1 mm thick), parallel-plate electrodes (30 nm Pt / 50 nm Au), free-space fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer at 1550 nm, 100 kHz drive (p.8 Methods); no waveguide or modulator device. PAPER-REPORTED MATERIAL NUMBERS (no column; all measured, bias-induced Pockels effect, T = 5 K or temperature of maximum with T < 10 K, 1550 nm, 100 kHz, Table I p.6): r33,max 580(60) / 840(50) / 1150(30) pm/V for natural STO / STO-28 (28% 18O) / STO-33 (33% 18O); d33,max 91(6) / 150(9) / 435(25) pC/N (authors give these as lower bounds, LN control read 4.6 vs known 6 pm/V, p.8-9); eps_r,max 26.0(1.5)k / 42.0(3.7)k / 82.0(1.6)k (LCR meter, 100 kHz, 1 V, p.8); field of max r33 0.080 / 0.036 / 0.008 MV/m; g11 0.15(2) / 0.21(3) / 0.30(1) m^4/C^2; q11 0.024(3) / 0.039(6) / 0.110(7) m^4/C^2; (P*eps_r)max 200(20) / 145(20) / 164(5) C/m^2; k33,max 0.15(1) / 0.21(2) / 0.46(3). Abstract: r33 exceeding 500 pm/V at 5 K (natural STO), above 1100 pm/V for STO-33. Fig. 4(a) p.6 gives the field dependence. Other: natural-STO low-frequency eps_r above 25,000 at low T (p.3, Fig. 2a); index 2.284 at 1550 nm (p.3); r13 = 170(20) pm/V, r33/r13 about 3.33 (Supplement S4, p.16); s11 at least 5e-15 m^2/V^2 (p.4); LN control r33 about 31 and r13 about 9 pm/V (p.8); bulk STO loss: intrinsic 0-0.2 dB/cm upper limit at room temperature, about 0.7 dB/cm saturated at low T, about 0.9 dB/cm peak near 75 V, below 0.55 dB/cm at 200 V (Supplement S8, p.18-19, Fig. S8); electro-optic bandwidth above 1 THz is a prediction from the Lyddane-Sachs-Teller relation (Supplement S6, p.18, predicted, not measured); measured RC cutoff about 1-4 MHz limited by sample capacitance (Supplement S5, p.17). Literature comparison values quoted in the text (LN r33 about 24 pm/V, BTO r42 about 170 pm/V at cryogenic T) are not this paper's measurements. No fabricator or wafer supplier named for the commercial STO chips; Stanford Nano Shared Facilities appears as an author affiliation (NanoSIMS isotope check).

papers.label: Guo et al. 2026
papers.notes: VERSION: all numbers come from the cached arXiv v2 preprint (2603.14346v2, 16 pp, no date stamp, no journal DOI located; no crossref.json); license and published_on empty. Supplemental Notes 1-3 not cached. Identity: title and 12 authors match the batch CSV (the CSV list is truncated). Two rows: guo2026-a, the 3 mm push-pull CLTW MZM at 532 nm (headline, UWOC transmitter), and guo2026-b, the dual-drive MZM used for optical single-sideband and EO comb generation (no Vpi or bandwidth reported). repro_grade C and no sim config: substrate not stated, propagation direction not stated, and the CLTW parameters (g, r, c, s, t, h) = (3.5, 45, 5, 2, 2, 3.5) um are defined only by the unlabeled top-view schematic of Fig. 2(a) (the text does not define the letters and the sketch does not make clear which of g and h, both 3.5 um, is the electrode-to-waveguide gap vs the stem length), so the loaded and unloaded cross-sections cannot be built without guessing which letter is the electrode-to-waveguide gap; electrode_gap_um is therefore left empty. Judgment calls: Vpi 2.6 V (100 kHz sawtooth, Fig. 5(b)) and Vpi*L 0.78 V cm (the authors compute it from Vpi and the 3 mm length, so basis derived; simulated 0.77 V cm in notes) entered with approx because the paper writes about-equal; bandwidth ~50 GHz is a bound (gt): the intro says exceeds 50 GHz, the trace in Fig. 5(d) spans about 3 to 57 GHz with large ripple, touches -3 dB at about 33, 36, 48 and 56 GHz relative to a baseline near +1 dB, and the authors blame the visible photodiode; the 57 GHz end is read from the plot. ER entered as >35 dB static from the text and the Fig. 5(c) label; the Fig. 5(c) caption says ~32 dB (inconsistent); Fig. 5(c) peak about -21 dBm and null about -56 dBm. On-chip IL 2.7 dB is the authors subtraction of grating-coupler loss from about 12 dB fiber-to-fiber (12 minus 2 x 4.5 is 3.0, so the implied per-coupler loss is about 4.65 dB). Propagation loss 1.7 read from Fig. 4(b) for the 1.5 um width (y-axis labeled dB, text says dB/cm). RF values (loss about 5.5 dB/cm at 100 GHz, n_RF about 2.48, Z0 about 49 ohm, ng about 2.45) are simulated CLTW design values read at 100 GHz from Fig. 3 / text. Optical handling: stable for 1 h at 18 dBm input / >5 dBm output, quoted as about 11.5 dBm on-chip (the authors' own deduction, the paper shows no derivation, and the top of the tested range rather than a measured limit; basis author_estimate); a TFLN comparison device fluctuated above 10 dBm input. max_baud_gbd 100 is derived from 100 Gb/s OOK (1 bit per symbol); the PAM-4 point is 56 GBd, 112 Gb/s over 3 m; 64 Gb/s OOK over 9 m; BER threshold 3.8e-3; system limited by AWG/oscilloscope/photodiode, not the chip (authors). Not reported: substrate, wafer supplier, foundry (device fabricated in-house, facility not named), optical input power of the Vpi measurement, drive amplitude of the UWOC runs (SHF 807c saturates at about 6 Vpp), energy per bit. TO phase shifter 0.51 mm, P_pi about 50 mW. Batch CSV hints (flat to about 50 GHz, 112 Gb/s over 3 m, 64 Gb/s over 9 m) verified. Audit corrections 2026-10-03: see AUDIT_DISPOSITIONS.md.
